typicalApplication: In the typical solar charger application, VCC is fed from the photovoltaic panel through a Schottky blocking diode (D1) and bypassed to GND with an electrolytic bulk capacitor plus a 1–10 µF ceramic and a 47 nF–1 µF high-frequency capacitor (C1/C2). VG is the internal gate-drive supply and is connected to VCC via a 100 nF capacitor. DRV drives the gate of an external P-channel MOSFET (M1) whose source is tied to VCC and drain to the inductor L; the other end of L connects to the current sense resistor RCS and then to the BAT node. A catch Schottky diode (D2) is placed from the inductor/BAT node back to ground as shown. CSP connects to the inductor side of RCS and BAT connects to the battery side of RCS, providing Kelvin-sensed current measurement. The BAT node is also connected to the positive terminal of the single-cell Li-ion battery and to the output capacitor bank (C3/C4) to GND. COM is connected to GND through a series network of 220 nF and 120 Ω for loop compensation. MPPT is tied to a resistor divider (R3/R4) from the panel input (VCC) to GND so that the MPPT pin is regulated to 1.205 V at the desired panel maximum power point voltage. CHRG and DONE are open-drain outputs that typically drive red and green LEDs (with series resistors) to VCC to indicate charging and charge termination, or can be pulled up to a logic rail for status monitoring. GND is the common return for the IC, sense resistor, input and output capacitors, and diodes, with careful layout to minimize switching noise.

typicalApplication: High-speed CAN transceiver. VDD (pin 3) needs 4.5-5.5 V with a 100 nF decoupler to VSS (pin 2). TXD (pin 1) and RXD (pin 4) go to the controller's CAN peripheral; TXD carries an internal 25 kOhm pull-up so a floating input leaves the bus recessive. CANH (pin 7) and CANL (pin 6) are the differential bus and take a 120 Ohm termination at each physical end of the cable only. description: Serial 8-digit LED display driver, 5V, up to 64 LEDs
firmwareNotes: Use SPI up to 10MHz; write 16-bit frames (address + data) to update digits; configure decode mode and intensity before use.

companions.notes: 0.1µF ceramic close to V+ and GND as per datasheet
10µF electrolytic/ceramic bulk cap near V+ for LED driver
Optional pull-up on DIN for shared-bus designs
Optional pull-up on CLK for shared-bus designs
Optional pull-up on LOAD/CS for defined idle state

typicalApplication: Connect V+ to a regulated +5V supply with a 0.1µF ceramic and 10µF electrolytic capacitor to GND placed close to the device; tie both GND pins to the ground plane. Drive the serial interface from a microcontroller by wiring DIN to a MOSI/GPIO output, CLK to an SPI SCK/GPIO clock, and LOAD to a chip-select/latched-load GPIO; DOUT can be wired to DIN of a second MAX7219 for cascading. Connect DIG0–DIG7 outputs to the common-cathode lines of up to eight 7-segment or LED-matrix digits, and connect SEG A–SEG G and SEG DP outputs to the corresponding segment/anode lines across all digits. Set the LED segment current by connecting a resistor (typically 9.53kΩ for about 40mA segment current) from V+ to ISET. The microcontroller programs decode mode, intensity, scan limit, shutdown, and digit data via 16-bit serial writes to the internal registers.

notes: Pin sides are inferred from the top-view pin diagram; exact KiCad symbol name approximated.
Operating current: 8mA taken from PD equation term (V+ x 8mA) as typical supply current; datasheet also lists 320–330mA including LED load.
SPI mode is not explicitly stated; default 0 assumed as common for MAX7219 libraries.
Package chosen as DIP-24 per ordering info; SO-24 variants also exist but archetype likely uses DIP.

description: Dual voltage comparator, 2–30 V supply, open-collector outputs
firmwareNotes: Analog comparator with open-collector outputs; requires pull-ups on OUT pins.

companions.notes: 100 nF ceramic close to VCC-GND

typicalApplication: LM393 is wired as two independent comparators powered from a single supply between 2 V and 30 V. VCC (pin 8) connects to the system supply with a 100 nF decoupling capacitor to GND (pin 4). Each comparator uses 1IN+ (pin 3) and 1IN− (pin 2) for the first channel and 2IN+ (pin 5) and 2IN− (pin 6) for the second channel; these pins are driven by the reference voltage and the sensed signal, often with resistor dividers. Outputs 1OUT (pin 1) and 2OUT (pin 7) are open-collector and require pull-up resistors to the desired logic or supply rail; they can sink up to about 4–6 mA and interface to TTL/CMOS or analog loads. The ground pin is the common reference for inputs and outputs, and the input common-mode range extends from GND up to approximately VCC−2 V.

notes: Package chosen as SOIC-8; LM393 is also available in PDIP-8 and SO-8, but one footprint had to be selected.
CurrentTypMa and currentMaxMa taken from LM393 electrical characteristics table (ICC at 5 V and 30 V).

description: Dual low-voltage rail-to-rail output op amp, 2.7–5.5 V, 1 MHz
firmwareNotes: Analog dual op amp, no digital interface

companions.notes: 100 nF ceramic close to VCC+ and GND

typicalApplication: LMV358 is used as a dual low-voltage op amp with VCC+ connected to a 2.7–5.5 V supply and GND to ground. Each amplifier is wired in standard op-amp configurations: for example, the first channel uses 1IN+ as the noninverting input tied to a reference or signal source, 1IN– connected to a feedback network from OUT (pin 1) and the input signal, forming an inverting or noninverting gain stage. The second channel similarly uses 2IN+ and 2IN– with feedback to 2OUT (pin 7). A 100 nF bypass capacitor is placed between VCC+ (pin 8) and GND (pin 4) close to the device. Outputs drive resistive or mixed loads within the specified output swing and load resistance limits.

notes: Package chosen as SOIC-8; LMV358 is also available in VSSOP and TSSOP variants.
Typical and max supply currents taken from LMV358I (both amplifiers) at VCC=5 V, TA=25°C and TA range.

description: Dual low-noise JFET-input op amp, ±2.25V to ±20V supply
firmwareNotes: Analog dual op amp; no digital interface.

companions.notes: 100nF ceramic from VCC+ to VCC– placed close to the IC

typicalApplication: TL072 is wired as two independent op-amp stages. Pin 4 (VCC–) and pin 8 (VCC+) connect to the negative and positive supply rails respectively, with a 100nF bypass capacitor between them near the device. Each amplifier uses its noninverting input (1IN+ on pin 3, 2IN+ on pin 5) and inverting input (1IN– on pin 2, 2IN– on pin 6) configured per the desired topology (for example, in a noninverting audio buffer, the input signal is fed to the noninverting input, a feedback resistor is placed from the output to the inverting input, and another resistor from the inverting input to a reference node). Outputs 1OUT (pin 1) and 2OUT (pin 7) drive the load or subsequent stages, typically through coupling components such as resistors or capacitors depending on the audio signal path.
